text:
Sam: Quick sync — we need to pick the internal API shape for inference routing. grpc-first backend + a tiny JSON gateway for external clients vs a gateway-forwarding approach that hides transport. Main open items: quota enforcement location, trace/attr propagation, and rollout UX. @Maya @Tomas any hot takes?
Maya: grpc-first still my vote. simpler types, streaming for long responses, and easier to maintain model stubs. but we need a thin JSON adapter for browser/workers.
Tomas: agree on grpc for backend. my worry: if we push quota logic into the runtime, we duplicate logic across runtimes (py/cc/rust) and we lose a single enforcement point for policy.
Jin: duplication is painful but avoids a central latency/availability choke. gateway-based enforcement introduces single hop failure mode.
Priya: middle ground — gateway enforces coarse quotas (reject blatantly over-limit requests), runtime does fine-grained accounting and final enforcement. gateway attaches an enforcement hint header so runtimes can reconcile.
Ben: +1. also need to ensure telemetry/trace identity flows from gateway -> runtime -> model shards. otherwise console metrics will be fragmented. we must propagate: x-request-id, x-redwood-tenant, x-trace, x-quota-hint.
Ben: example header propagation we should standardize on (pseudo):
```
X-Request-Id: 7f3b9c
X-Redwood-Tenant: org_17
X-Trace-Context: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
X-Quota-Hint: precheck=20/1000
```
Zoe: console needs to show the mismatch between gateway prechecks and runtime actuals. a per-route quota breakdown and a small "reconcile drift" panel would help SRE debug.
Maya: about the JSON adapter — let's keep it stateless and tiny. mapping example: client JSON -> grpc proto request. if we do this as a sidecar or Envoy filter we can avoid a separate service. snippet (psuedo):
```
{"input_text":"..."} -> PredictRequest { prompt: "...", max_tokens: 256 }
```
Tomas: Envoy filter is attractive for speed, but it complicates schema evolution on the filter side. if proto changes we need coordinated filter updates.
Priya: rollout UX idea: deploy gateway+filter in canary 10% traffic, enable precheck mode where gateway marks prechecks but doesn't reject. collect metrics for 24h, then flip to enforced if signals look good. ops-bot can automate.
ops-bot: Canary job queued: `./deploy --service=gateway --env=staging --canary=10% --monitor=24h`. Use `--dry-run` to simulate.
Jin: metrics to watch: 1) false rejects (gateway rejects but runtime accepts) 2) latency p50/p95 delta introduced by gateway 3) reconciled quota drift per tenant.
Zoe: add UX for rollback: per-canary toggle in console (one-click rollback and an automated fallback route to legacy runtime). also show a small heatmap of tenant impact.
Ben: one more: auth scopes. gateway should forward scoped tokens but not mint scopes. runtime should validate scopes against its local policy cache. otherwise audits get messy.
Sam: OK next steps: (1) doc the header contract (Ben), (2) prototype Envoy filter adapter + a sidecar JSON -> grpc translator (Maya/Jin), (3) implement gateway precheck header and telemetry instrumentation (Priya/Zoe), (4) ops run the canary with `--dry-run` and then enforce. I'll open a short RFC with these bullets. thanks all :thumbsup:
